metadata.title: BFS vs DFS: The Frontier Is the Algorithm

beats.new_visual_element: ROLE HOOK · BrutalistHesitantWriter; silent mystery question, zero static card.

props.text:
Search is search?
Same graph, same start…
why does the frontier change the answer?

beats.narration_text: Start at S. Breadth first removes the oldest frontier node, A, then B. The target T waits only two edges away, so it is reached before either deep branch.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Start at S. Breadth first removes the oldest frontier node, A, then B. The target T waits only two edges away, so it is reached before either deep branch.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 1 · Complete BFS trace; graph left, FIFO queue and visited order right.

beats.narration_text: Reset the same graph. Depth first removes the newest node, A, then C, then E, then F. It commits to one branch while the nearby target still waits.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Reset the same graph. Depth first removes the newest node, A, then C, then E, then F. It commits to one branch while the nearby target still waits.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 2 · Complete DFS trace; same graph, LIFO stack and visited order right.

beats.narration_text: Freeze here: the frontier holds B and C. A queue removes B; a stack removes C. Which node reaches the target sooner? Commit before the containers move.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Freeze here: the frontier holds B and C. A queue removes B; a stack removes C. Which node reaches the target sooner? Commit before the containers move.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PREDICT · Held graph plus hai-simple write-on question over yellow fill-only wash.

beats.narration_text: Change only the container. FIFO pulls from the old end and visits B, then T. LIFO pulls from the new end and follows C, E, F before returning.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Change only the container. FIFO pulls from the old end and visits B, then T. LIFO pulls from the new end and follows C, E, F before returning.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRANSFORM / TRACE · Queue morphs to stack while graph stays fixed; removal arrows move.

beats.narration_text: Try a wider graph. Breadth first empties every distance-one node before any distance-two node. Depth first still follows whichever branch was pushed last.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Try a wider graph. Breadth first empties every distance one node before any distance two node. Depth first still follows whichever branch was pushed last.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 3 · Parametrized wider graph runs with explicit distance and branch labels.

beats.narration_text: Now the licensing characteristic is visible: unweighted edges make each step equal, and FIFO keeps the frontier in just two adjacent distance layers, d and d plus one.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Now the licensing characteristic is visible: unweighted edges make each step equal, and first in first out keeps the frontier in just two adjacent distance layers, d and d plus one.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE ABSTRACTION · Names unweighted equal-cost edges and FIFO two-layer frontier after three instances.

beats.narration_text: Why can no shorter route appear later? Every node entering layer d plus one came from layer d, and the queue finishes layer d before removing anything deeper.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Why can no shorter route appear later? Every node entering layer d plus one came from layer d, and the queue finishes layer d before removing anything deeper.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INVARIANT / PROOF · Nodes flow from layer d to d plus one while FIFO drains the earlier layer.

beats.narration_text: Return to the opening graph. BFS reaches T after S, A, B; DFS reaches it after S, A, C, E, F, B. Same graph, different frontier, different promise.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Return to the opening graph. B F S reaches T after S, A, B; D F S reaches it after S, A, C, E, F, B. Same graph, different frontier, different promise.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PAYOFF · Hook graph returns with both explicit visit sequences and target positions.

beats.narration_text: The verdict: queue means breadth and shortest unweighted distance. Stack means depth and a current path. Both traverse; only FIFO protects layers.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The verdict: queue means breadth and shortest unweighted distance. Stack means depth and a current path. Both traverse; only first in first out protects layers.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE VERDICT · ClaudeVerdictArtifact recap from the film's graph and containers.

artifactLines: Both traverse. Only FIFO protects layers.
